stem: A client is prescribed insulin glargine (LANTUS) as basal insulin. Which administration teaching is correct?

options.A: Inject it subcutaneously once daily at any time of day, but at the same time every day
options.B: Use it only as a rapid mealtime bolus when carbohydrate intake is high
options.C: Give it intravenously for acute diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Mix it in the same syringe with another insulin before each dose

rationale: Current LANTUS labeling states that insulin glargine is administered subcutaneously once daily at any time of day, but at the same time each day. It is a long-acting basal insulin rather than a rapid mealtime insulin, it is not recommended for treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis, and the label instructs not to dilute or mix LANTUS with another insulin or solution. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Teach correct basal insulin glargine administration: once-daily subcutaneous dosing at a consistent daily time, without mixing it with other insulins.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_locator: §2.1 General Dosing Instructions: administer subcutaneously once daily at any time of day but at the same time every day; do not dilute or mix with other insulin/solution. §1 Limitations of Use: not recommended for treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis
source_claim_supported: LANTUS is a once-daily subcutaneous basal insulin administered at the same time each day; it should not be mixed with other insulin and is not DKA therapy.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — safe medication administration, medication-related client education, and evaluation of medication therapy
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — basal insulin glargine administration
correction_summary: Replaced insulin detemir/LEVEMIR because Novo Nordisk lists LEVEMIR as no longer available in the U.S. Rebuilt the item around currently available insulin glargine and pinned dosing/mixing instructions to current DailyMed labeling.
audit_findings: A is the exact labeled administration pattern. B describes prandial insulin use; C conflicts with the DKA limitation; D conflicts with the no-mixing instruction. The item avoids dose calculations or conversion rules and has one clear best answer. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
